headline: Medium prompt-injection, data-leakage, and cascading-error risks from file-based document parsing into audio transcription; no direct shared channel is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A reads and writes documents, while agent B consumes audio files only; no direct shared channel is documented, so prompt injection is not provably absent. If A’s document outputs are copied into B’s prompts or transcripts, malicious instructions could ride along. The pair lacks explicit provenance or filtering, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF A’s document output is manually pasted into B’s prompt or transcript input, injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared workspace is introduced between the agents, the attack surface expands.
mitigations: Keep A and B on separate workspaces.
Do not paste A outputs into B prompts.
Add a provenance tag to any handoff text.
Review any shared transcript before reuse.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization at the handoff boundary.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A can read and write documents and has allowlisted egress, while B has no network egress and cannot read filesystems. The pair does not show a shared workspace or shared credentials, so leakage is limited and not default. The main risk is operator-mediated transfer of sensitive document text from A into B’s audio workflow.
conditions: IF sensitive document text from A is copied into B’s inputs, that text may be exposed in downstream artifacts.
IF both agents are pointed at the same directory, leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Use separate input directories.
Avoid copying document text into audio jobs.
Redact sensitive fields before handoff.
Confirm B remains offline.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation in the orchestrator.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses; B cannot write files, modify git, or spawn subprocesses. There is no overlapping write surface or shared mutable resource in the profiles, so direct capability conflict is unlikely. Any conflict would require an external orchestrator to map both onto the same writable path, which is not documented here.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator gives both agents the same writable directory, file clobbering becomes possible.
IF B is wrapped with additional write tools, the conflict profile changes.
mitigations: Assign distinct output paths.
Disable any shared temp directory.
Run A and B in separate containers.
Check for accidental symlink reuse.
requires-engineering: add lockfiles for any shared mutable resource.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A produces parsed document content, and B is a speech model that could be fed A’s text as a transcript or prompt by an operator. B does not verify document facts, so if A’s output is treated as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream speech artifacts. The interaction is inferred rather than directly documented, so uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF A’s extracted text is used as source material for B without verification, errors can propagate.
IF B’s output is later treated as factual content, the cascade widens.
mitigations: Insert a human verification step.
Compare A output against source documents.
Label A output as untrusted.
Keep B limited to transcription, not factual synthesis.
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks between stages.

E_compliance.rationale: A touches documents and images and may call external APIs, while B is offline and file-only for audio. No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented, so compliance risk is limited to whatever sensitive document class A processes. B is not cited for residency because its profile shows no outbound data flow or regulated-data handling beyond local audio files.
conditions: IF A processes regulated documents and sends them to external APIs, residency or retention obligations may apply.
IF audio inputs contain regulated content and are stored outside policy, compliance risk increases.
mitigations: Classify inputs before processing.
Avoid regulated documents in A.
Keep B offline and local.
Review retention settings for A’s API calls.
requires-engineering: document a data-processing agreement and retention policy.
